methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $70M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Climate & Energy. Range: $700M - $3.0B.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Neustark is a Series B-stage climate and energy company that has raised $70M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of 9 private companies and 1 public company (Lnza) operating in the same sector and stage band, including peers such as KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Amogy.

Two valuation methods are applicable. Stage-progression analysis uses the $70M total raised as a proxy for post-money valuation and applies a typical 1.9x step-up multiplier from Series B to the next funding stage, yielding $133M. Peer-median analysis identifies three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables (KoBold Metals at $3.0B, Electric Hydrogen at $1.0B, and Amogy at $700M), producing a median valuation of $1.0B and a range of $700M to $3.0B.

Triangulation of these two methods produces a low estimate of $113M, a median of $566M, and a high of $1.1B. The wide range reflects material uncertainty around comparable company selection—peer valuations span nearly 4x—and the early-stage nature of the climate-tech sector, where growth trajectories and commercial viability remain unproven. The stage-progression method anchors conservatively to deployed capital; the peer method incorporates later-stage funding and market appetite but may overstate Neustark's position relative to more mature peers.
